title: Glossary of the Digital Transformation Handbook for Health Product Catalogue
description: The handbook's own product catalogue terms, one concept per term, each quoting the handbook with its L1 page. KG concepts are written Capitalized (owner, 2026-10-31). Supply chain terms (traceability, the foundational components, order and warehouse management) are held in dth-sc, which dth-pc depends on; general digital terms (registry, interoperability, open standards, …) in smart-ra, with this handbook's wording as a cited alternative (litlfred/smart-ra#142). Every term is a candidate: only a person adopts a definition. When the smart-ra and dth-sc schemes are mounted, each term gains closeMatch/broadMatch links to the concept it narrows. Scope: the handbook does not cover medical devices (page 16); nothing here extends to them (owner, 2026-10-31, workplan Q4).

terms.definition: Product master data consists of standardized information that accurately describes a health product’s characteristics. This data remains consistent across all instances of a product.
terms.scopeNote: Handbook wording, quoted. A candidate: not adopted, nothing chosen between alternatives. Examples the handbook gives: product description, dosage, pharmaceutical strength, manufacturer details, shelf life. Owner, 2026-10-31: one concept, no homonym split with the RA's 'Product'. Not defined in dth-sc; this handbook is its source.

terms.definition: In contrast, transactional data—such as batch numbers, manufacturing dates, and serial numbers—varies with each specific instance of the product.
terms.scopeNote: Handbook wording, quoted. A candidate: not adopted, nothing chosen between alternatives. Defined by contrast with Product Master Data.

terms.definition: In this handbook, the terms ‘generic product,’ ‘product,’ or ‘product information’ pertain to the general identifying details of a health product, excluding any manufacturer-specific information.
terms.scopeNote: Handbook wording, quoted. A candidate: not adopted, nothing chosen between alternatives. Alternative wording in Ch 2 (page 28): 'Generic products can be described as generic items that conceal the brand or manufacturer information.' Countries identify them with generic national product codes.

terms.definition: Trade items are manufacturer-specific branded health products that are identifiable and unique to a particular brand or manufacturer.
terms.scopeNote: Handbook wording, quoted (Ch 2, page 28). A candidate: not adopted. Owner ruling 2026-10-31: Trade Item is the WHO concept, with this narrow sense; the GS1 trade item is a separate external concept and the WHO term's broadMatch (every WHO Trade Item is a GS1 trade item, not the reverse: GS1's also covers services). The handbook's glossary (page 9) prints the GS1 wording, 'Products or services that are priced, ordered or invoiced at any point in the supply chain', citing GS1 (its reference 13); that sentence is GS1's definition, recorded here as a note, not as this concept's. litlfred/smart-ra#142 item 1.

terms.definition: A Regulated Trade Item represents an authorization of a Trade item within a given jurisdiction under a Product Authorization.
terms.scopeNote: Handbook wording, quoted. A candidate: not adopted, nothing chosen between alternatives. Its attributes and cardinalities are in Fig 9 (page 29): identifier 1..*, jurisdiction 1..*, authorisationHolder 1..1, authorisedTradeItem 1..1.

terms.definition: Classifications such as the anatomical therapeutic chemical classification system with defined daily doses (ATC/DDD) and the international statistical classification of diseases (ICD) categorize diseases, pathogens, or health products to assist with morbidity and mortality statistics and support healthcare decision-making.
terms.scopeNote: Handbook wording, quoted. A candidate: not adopted, nothing chosen between alternatives. Defined by example. Fig 8 places it above Generic Product and Trade Item (strategic, tactical, operational use).

terms.definition: Adopting a suitable technology tool supports the ongoing management of product master data while maintaining consistent quality and compliance with defined standards. A widely used term for such a tool is the NPC, which many countries implement to oversee product master data.
terms.scopeNote: Handbook wording, quoted. A candidate: not adopted, nothing chosen between alternatives. The handbook names the TOOL the NPC; it realises the Product Registry foundational component of the dth-sc DHSC architecture (page 16). Link target in smart-ra: Product Catalog Management System / Product Registry.

terms.definition: This attribute is designed to default to GTINs when they are available. In the absence of GTINs, the attribute generates and maintains a local identifier, which can be replaced with a GTIN once it is assigned to the trade item.
terms.scopeNote: Handbook wording, quoted. A candidate: not adopted, nothing chosen between alternatives. A local identifier attribute for Trade Items without a GTIN (Fig 13, page 40).

terms.definition: Data owner: responsible for the overall strategy, governance, and quality of the product master data.
terms.scopeNote: Handbook wording, quoted. A candidate: not adopted, nothing chosen between alternatives. One of three illustrative data management roles.

terms.definition: Data custodian: responsible for the technical management and security of product master data.
terms.scopeNote: Handbook wording, quoted. A candidate: not adopted, nothing chosen between alternatives. One of three illustrative data management roles.

terms.definition: Data steward: responsible for the day-to-day management, maintenance, and quality control of the product master data.
terms.scopeNote: Handbook wording, quoted. A candidate: not adopted, nothing chosen between alternatives. One of three illustrative data management roles.

terms.definition: Establish a master data governance group composed of all relevant stakeholders to provide leadership and guidance in managing product master data additions and changes.
terms.scopeNote: Handbook wording, quoted. A candidate: not adopted, nothing chosen between alternatives. Worded as an instruction; the group is what it creates.
Named as an example role ('Catalogue Manager, NPC System Administrator') with a role description listed as a resource; the handbook prints no definition.
terms.reason: Named only; the role description is a resource the handbook lists but does not print.

terms.scopeNote: Used with Fig 10 (primary, secondary, tertiary levels, from GS1) and Fig 11–12 (pack configurations across manufacturers); the handbook gives no defining sentence.
terms.reason: Shown in figures, never defined in text.

terms.scopeNote: An open-source tool (PCMT) the handbook recommends considering for the NPC, with a WHO-hosted instance (Ch 6). A named product, so not defined here; smart-pcmt is downstream of dth-pc.
terms.reason: A named software product, not a concept the handbook defines.

terms.scopeNote: Used in Fig 8 and Fig 9 (generic product attribute unitOfUse 1..1) and Fig 14 ('Unit of use'), never defined in text. smart-pcmt's PCMTGlossary has '#unitOfUse "The base unit to count by"'; that CodeSystem is to be retired in favour of this term (litlfred/smart-ra#145).
terms.reason: Shown only as a model attribute; the handbook gives no defining sentence.
